title: INDIA Bloc Marches on Ramlila Maidan Demanding Election Chief's Resignation
excerpt: Rahul Gandhi led the 'Chalo Dilli' march from Connaught Place on Sunday, accusing the Election Commission of irregularities in the voter-roll revision, as the BJP called the rally a threat to Delhi's festive trade.
body:
• The INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' march and rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, November 1, protesting alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
  • The alliance's central demand is the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
  • Delhi Police deployed personnel from multiple agencies, imposed Section 163 BNSS restrictions, and announced traffic curbs around the venue; the rally had permission but was asked to end by evening.
  • Union minister J.P. Nadda attacked the rally as insensitive and damaging to festive-season trade, while Rahul Gandhi urged participants to shop at small local businesses.

Thousands of opposition supporters marched through central Delhi on Sunday as the INDIA bloc turned its campaign against the Election Commission into a street protest, culminating in a rally at Ramlila Maidan. Led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, the 'Chalo Dilli' march set out from Connaught Place at noon and moved towards the ground via Ajmeri Gate, according to IANS reporting carried by Hi India.

"Delhi, get ready! Save the Vote, Save the Nation. Come to Connaught Place, let's march together. Or meet directly at Ramlila Maidan — but you must come."

— Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, in a post on X

What the opposition is demanding

The alliance organised the gathering around three demands: action against alleged irregularities in the ongoing electoral roll revision, opposition to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) being conducted by the Election Commission of India, and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut described the event as a 'mega rally' and said the agitation would continue until the Chief Election Commissioner stepped down. Gandhi had alleged that people were being stopped from joining the rally, a claim Nation Press noted could not be independently verified.

https://x.com/htTweets/status/2116817421822808328

The SIR — a door-to-door re-verification of voter lists — has become the opposition's main line of attack on the poll body this year, with Congress alleging that the revision is being used to remove legitimate voters. The Election Commission has previously defended the exercise as a routine clean-up of the rolls; the rally is the campaign's largest Delhi show of strength so far.

Heavy security and traffic curbs

Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was in force across Delhi districts, with gatherings prohibited at locations including Jantar Mantar and the Election Commission office. Personnel from the Rapid Action Force, CISF, CRPF and SSB were deployed alongside Delhi Police around Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg, and traffic curbs were announced ahead of the march. Delhi Police said permission for the rally had been granted but that Congress had not informed it of the march, ANI reported via the Daily Jagran, and the alliance was asked to end the demonstration by evening.

The INDIA bloc projected participation of nearly 10 lakh people, an expectation reported ahead of the event; police planning was based on roughly 50,000 people, in line with the ground's capacity. Neither figure is a count of who actually attended.

The BJP's counter-attack

Union minister J.P. Nadda led the government's response, calling the rally an attempt to push the country into disorder under the cover of democracy. He said the November 1 date was insensitive because it marks the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence. Nadda also cited a letter from the Chamber of Trade and Industry urging opposition leaders not to hold large programmes in Delhi during the festive period, and claimed earlier protests had cost Delhi traders about Rs 3,000 crore, with losses from this event potentially exceeding Rs 10,000 crore — figures he asserted and which have not been independently established.

Gandhi, for his part, appealed to people travelling to the capital to support local traders by shopping at small businesses during the festive season, a message aimed at blunting the trade argument.

What happens next

Raut's warning that the agitation continues until the CEC resigns sets up a longer confrontation over the SIR, which is under way in poll-bound states. Whether the alliance can sustain street pressure — and whether the Election Commission responds to the resignation demand — will shape the next phase of the voter-roll fight.
nri_angle: The rally escalates the opposition's campaign over voter-roll revisions ahead of state polls, a fight diaspora voters are watching for what it signals about India's electoral process.
